translations.text: Moab rebelled against the king of Israel after Ahab died.
Ahaziah fell from the balcony of his upper room in Samaria and became ill. He sent messengers and told them, “Go and ask Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this illness.”

The angel of the LORD said to Elijah from Tishbe, “Get up and go down to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria. Say to them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?’”
“Therefore, this is what the LORD says: ‘You will not come down from the bed you have climbed into, but you will certainly die.’” Then Elijah went away.
The messengers returned to Ahaziah, and Ahaziah said to them, “Why have you returned?”

They said to him, “A man came up to meet us and told us, ‘Turn back and go to the man who sent you. Tell him: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore, this is what the LORD says: You will not come down from the bed you have climbed into, but you will certainly die.’”
He said to them, “What did the man who came up to meet you and said these things to you look like?”
They said to him, “He was a hairy man, with a leather belt tied around his waist.” He said to them, “It is Elijah from Tishbe.”
He sent a captain of fifty with his fifty men against Elijah. They went up to him as he was sitting on the mountaintop. The captain said to him, “Prophet of God, the king says, ‘Come down!’”

Elijah answered the captain of fifty, “If I am a prophet of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.” Then fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.
Again he sent another captain of fifty with his fifty men against Elijah. The captain spoke to him and said, “Prophet of God, this is what the king says: ‘Come down quickly!’”
Elijah answered him, “If I am a prophet of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty men.” Then the fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.

For a third time he sent a captain of fifty with his fifty men against Elijah. The captain of fifty went up, knelt before Elijah, and pleaded with him, saying, “Prophet of God, let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours who stand before you be precious to you.
Look, fire came down from heaven and consumed the two captains of fifty and their fifty men each. But now, let my life be precious in your eyes.”
The angel of the Lord said to Elijah, “Go down with him; do not be afraid of him.” So he got up and went down with him to the king.

He said to him, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because you sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron—is it because there is no God in Israel whose word you could seek?—therefore you will not come down from the bed you have climbed into, but you will certainly die.’”
He died according to the word of the LORD that Elijah had spoken. His brother Joram became king after him, in the second year of Joram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, because Ahaziah had no son.
The rest of the acts of Ahaziah and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
When the Lord was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha set out from Gilgal.

Elijah said to Elisha, “Stay here, please, because the LORD has sent me to Bethel.” But Elisha said, “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” So they went down to Bethel.
The members of the company of prophets at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, “Do you not know that today the LORD is taking your master away from over you?” He said, “I know too. Be quiet.”

Elijah said to Elisha, “Stay here, please, because the LORD has sent me to Jericho.” But he said, “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” So they went to Jericho.
The members of the company of prophets at Jericho approached Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that today the LORD is taking your master away from over you?” He said, “I know too. Be quiet.”

Elijah said to Elisha, “Stay here, please, because the LORD has sent me to the Jordan.” But he said, “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” So the two of them went on.
Fifty men from the company of prophets went and stood facing them at a distance, while the two of them stood on the bank of the Jordan.
Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the waters of the Jordan. They divided, half to one side and half to the other, and the two of them crossed on dry ground.
When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask what I can do for you before I am taken away from you.” Elisha said, “Let a double portion of your spirit rest on me.”
He said, “You have asked a great deal. If you see me as I am taken away from you, it will be so for you; but if not, it will not be.”
As they were walking and talking, suddenly a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them. Elijah went up to heaven in a whirlwind.
Elisha saw it and cried out, “My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!” Then he saw him no more. He took hold of his clothes and tore them into two pieces.
He picked up Elijah’s cloak, which had fallen from him, returned, and stood on the bank of the Jordan.
He called to the LORD and said, “Where is the LORD, the God of my master Elijah?” He too struck the waters of the Jordan, and they divided, half to one side and half to the other, and Elisha crossed.
The members of the prophetic community at Jericho saw him from a distance and said, “The spirit of Elijah has rested on Elisha.” They came to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

They said to him, “Look, there are fifty strong men here among your servants. Let them go and search for your master. Perhaps the Spirit of the Lord has lifted him up and thrown him onto one of the mountains or into one of the valleys.” He said, “Do not send them.”
They kept pressing him until he was embarrassed by them, and he said, “Send them.” So they sent fifty men, who searched for him for three days but did not find him.
They returned to him while he was staying in Jericho, and he said to them, “Did I not tell you not to go?”
The men of the town said to Elisha, “Look, the town’s location is pleasant, as our lord can see, but the water is bad and the land is barren.”
He said, “Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it.” So they brought it to him.
He went out to the spring of water, threw salt into it, and said, “This is what the Lord says: I have healed this water. No longer will there be death or miscarriage from it.”
The water has remained healed to this day, according to the word that Elisha spoke.
He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up the road, some little boys came out of the town and mocked him, saying, “Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!”
He turned around, saw them, and cursed them in the name of the Lord. Two female bears came out of the woods and tore apart forty-two of the boys.
He went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
Joram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned for twelve years.
He did what was evil before the Lord, though not like his father and mother. He removed the sacred pillar of Baal that his father had made.
Nevertheless, he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused Israel to sin, and did not turn away from them.
Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder. He used to deliver to the king of Israel a hundred thousand fat sheep and a hundred thousand rams with their wool.
After Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
King Joram went out from Samaria that day and mustered all Israel.

He sent word to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, saying, “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Come with me, and let us go to war against Moab.” Jehoshaphat said to him, “I will go up. I am as you are, my people are as your people, and my horses are as your horses.”
He said to him, “By which road shall we go up?” He answered, “By the road through the wilderness of Edom.”
The king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom set out. They made a roundabout journey of seven days, and there was no water for the army or for the people with them.
The king of Israel said, “Alas! Is this why the Lord has called these three kings together—to hand them over to Moab?”

Jehoshaphat said, “Is there no prophet of the Lord here through whom we can inquire about the Lord’s word?” One of the servants of the king of Israel answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He used to pour water over Elijah’s hands.”
Jehoshaphat said, “The word of the Lord is with him.” So the king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom went down to him.

Elisha said to the king of Israel, “What have I to do with you? Go to your father’s prophets and your mother’s prophets.” The king of Israel said to him, “Is this why the Lord has called these three kings together—to hand them over to Moab?”
Elisha said, “As the Lord Almighty lives, whom I serve, if I did not have regard for Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look toward you or even take notice of you.”
But now bring me a musician.” While the musician was playing, the hand of the LORD came upon him.
He said, “Let this valley be filled with pits.
“For this is what the Lord says: You will see neither wind nor rain, yet this valley will be filled with water, and you and your livestock will drink.”
This is a small thing in the LORD’s eyes; he will also hand the Moabites over to you.
“You will destroy every fortified town and every choice town. You will cut down every good tree, stop up every spring of water, and fill every good piece of land with stones.”
In the morning, when the offering was presented, water came from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
All the Moabites saw that the kings had come up to fight against them. They called out everyone old enough to wear a sword and older, and they took their stand at the border.
They rose early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water. From a distance, the Moabites saw the water looking red like blood.
They said, “This is blood! The kings have been utterly destroyed; they have killed one another. Now, Moab, to the plunder!”
They came to the camp of Israel, and the Israelites rose up and struck down the Moabites, who fled before them. The Israelites advanced into their territory and devastated Moab.

They demolished the towns. Each man threw his stone onto every good piece of land until they had filled it. They stopped up every spring of water and cut down every good tree, until the stones in the wall were left overturned. The slingers surrounded it and destroyed it.
When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, he took seven hundred swordsmen with him to break through to the king of Edom, but he could not.
He took his firstborn son, who was to reign after him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. Great wrath came upon Israel, and they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.

A woman, one of the wives of the prophets, cried out before Elisha, saying, “Your servant, my husband, has died. You know that your servant feared the Lord. Now the creditor has come to take my two sons as his slaves.”
Elisha said to her, “What can I do for you? Tell me what you have in the house.” She said, “Your servant has nothing in the house except a flask of oil.”
He said to her, “Go and borrow containers from outside, from all your neighbors—empty containers. Do not get just a few.
Then go inside and shut the door behind you and your sons. Pour water into all these containers, and bring the full container up to me.”
She left him, went inside, and shut the door behind herself and her sons. They brought the containers to her, and she poured.
When the containers were all used, she said to her son, “Bring me more containers.” Her son said to her, “There are no more containers.” Then the oil stopped flowing.
She came and told the prophet of God. He said to her, “Go, sell the oil and pay your debt. You and your sons can live on what remains.”
One day afterward, Elisha came and passed through Shiloh. There was a prominent woman there who urged him to eat a meal. Whenever he passed through, he would turn aside there to eat.
She said to her husband, “Look, I know that the prophet of God who regularly passes our way is holy.
“Let us prepare a small upstairs room for him and put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lampstand there for him. Then, whenever he comes to us, he can turn aside there.”
One day he came there, turned into the upstairs room, and lay down there.
He said to Gehazi his disciple, “Call this Shunammite woman.” He called her, and she stood before him.

He said to her, “You have taken all this trouble for us. What should be done for you? Is there something to be said on your behalf to the king or the commander of the army?” She said, “I live comfortably among my own people.”
He said, “What can I do for her?” Gehazi said to him, “She certainly has no son, and her husband is old.”
He said, “Call her.” He called her, and she stood in the doorway.
He said to her, “At this time, while you are still alive, you will embrace a son.” She said, “No, my lord, prophet of God! Do not lie to your servant.”
The woman conceived and gave birth to a son at that time, while she was alive, just as Elisha had told her.
The boy grew, and one day he went out to his father, to the reapers.
He said to his father, “My head! My head!” His father said to the servant, “Pick him up and take him to his mother.”
The servant picked him up and took him to his mother. He sat on her lap until noon and died.
She took him upstairs and laid him on the bed of the prophet of God. She shut the door behind him and went out.
She called her husband and said, “Send me one of the servants and a donkey, so I can go to the prophet of God.”
He said to her, “Why are you going to him today? It is neither the new moon nor the Sabbath.” And the Shunammite woman replied.
They put her on the donkey, and she said to the servant, “Drive it and go! Do not stop for me to rest unless I tell you.”
She went to the prophet of God at Mount Carmel. When the prophet of God saw her from a distance, he said to Gehazi his disciple, “Look, there is that woman from Shiloh.”
“Now run to meet her and say to her, ‘Are you well? Is your husband well? Is the boy well?’” She said, “All is well.”

She came to the prophet of God at Mount Carmel and took hold of his feet. Gehazi approached to pull her away, but the prophet of God said to him, “Leave her alone, for she is deeply distressed. The Lord has hidden it from me and has not told me.”
She said, “Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not tell you not to ask me?”
He said to Gehazi, “Tuck up your clothes, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer him. Lay my staff on the boy’s face.”
The boy’s mother said, “As the Lord lives and as you live, I will not leave you.” So he got up and followed her.
Gehazi went ahead of them and laid his staff on the boy’s face, but there was no sound or response. He returned to meet him and reported, “The boy has not awakened.”
Elisha came to the house and saw the boy lying dead on his bed.
He went in, shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed before the Lord.
He went up and lay on top of the boy, placing his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. He stretched himself over him, and the boy’s body grew warm.
He returned and walked back and forth in the house. Then he went up and stretched himself over him. The boy yawned seven times and opened his eyes.
He called Gehazi and said to him, “Call that woman from Shiloh.” He called her, and she came in to him. He said to her, “Take your son.”
She fell at his feet and bowed to him with her face to the ground. Then she took her son and went out.
Elisha returned to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land, and the prophets were sitting before him. He said to his disciple, “Put the large pot on the fire and cook a stew for the prophets.”

One of them went out into the field to gather herbs. He found a vine in the field and gathered a garmentful of wild gourds from it. He came and threw them into the stew pot, because he did not know what they were.
He served it to the men to eat. When they ate some of the stew, they said, “There is death in the pot, prophet of God!” They could not eat it.
He said, “Take some flour and throw it into the pot.” Then he said, “Serve it to the people so they can eat.” And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
A man came from the city of Ganbara and brought the prophet of God bread from the firstfruits: twenty barley loaves and crushed grain in a cloth. He said, “Give it to the people to eat.”
His attendant said to him, “How can I set this before a hundred men?” Elisha said to him, “Give it to the people to eat, for this is what the Lord says: ‘They will eat and have some left over.’”
He set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, according to the word of the Lord.

Naaman, the commander of the army of the king of Edom, was a great man in his master’s eyes and highly respected, because through him the Lord had given deliverance to Edom. Naaman was a mighty warrior, but he had leprosy.
The Edomites went out in raiding bands and took a young girl captive from the land of Israel. She served Naaman’s wife.
She said to her mistress, “If only my master would go to the prophet in Samaria! He would immediately cure him of his leprosy.”
They went in and told his master, saying to him, “This is what the girl from the land of Israel said.”
The king of Edom said to him, “Go ahead. I will send a letter to the king of Israel.” So he went, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten sets of clothes.
He brought the letter to the king of Israel. It read: “When this letter reaches you, I have sent you my servant Naaman. Cure him of his leprosy.”

When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, “Am I God, who puts to death and brings to life, that this man sends word to me to cure a man of his leprosy? Now understand and see that he is trying to pick a quarrel with me!”

When Elisha, the prophet of God, heard that the king had torn his clothes, he sent word to the king, saying, “Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel.”
Naaman came with his horses and his chariots and stopped at the entrance to Elisha’s house.
Elisha sent word to him through a messenger: “Go and wash seven times in the Jordan. Your flesh will be restored, and you will be clean.”

Naaman became angry and went away, saying, “I thought he would certainly come out to me, stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the affected place so that it would be healed of leprosy.”
“Are not Amana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? I could go and wash in them and be clean!” He turned and went away in a rage.

His servants approached and said to him, “Our master, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, would you not have had to do it? But look, he has told you to do something small: ‘Go, wash, and be clean.’”
He listened to them and did so. He went and washed seven times in the Jordan, and his flesh became like the flesh of a little boy, and he was clean.

He returned to the prophet of God with his entire company. He came and stood before him and said, “Now I know that there is no God anywhere on earth except in Israel. Now please accept this gift from your servant.”
Elisha said, “As the Lord lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept it.” Naaman urged him to accept it, but he refused.

Naaman said, “If not, then let your servant be given as much earth as two mules can carry, because your servant will no longer offer burnt offerings or sacrifices to any other god, but only to the LORD.”

“May the LORD forgive your servant in this matter: when my master enters the temple of Rimmon to worship there, leaning on my hands, and I bow down in the temple of Rimmon—when I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, may the LORD forgive your servant in this matter.”
He said to him, “Go in peace.” And he went away from him about a parasang.

Gehazi, the disciple of Elisha the prophet of God, said, “Look, my master has let this Edomite Naaman off without accepting anything he brought. As the LORD lives, I will run after him and take something from him.”
Gehazi ran after Naaman. When Naaman saw him running after him, he got down from his chariot to meet him and said, “Have you come with good news?”
He said, “All is well. My master sent me, saying, ‘Two men from the company of prophets have just come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Give them a talent of silver and two sets of clothes.’”
Naaman said, “Please, take two talents.” He urged him, tied up two talents in two cloths, along with two sets of clothes, and gave them to two of his young men, who carried them with him.
He came to [?], took the things from them, and stored them in the house. Then he sent the men away, and they left.
He came and stood before his master. Elisha said to him, “Where have you been, Gehazi?” He said, “Your servant has not gone anywhere.”

Elisha said to him, “My heart showed me when the man got down from his chariot to meet you. Is this the time to acquire silver and acquire clothes, olive groves, vineyards, sheep, cattle, male servants, and female servants?”
Naaman’s leprosy will cling to you and your descendants forever.” He went out from his presence leprous, like snow.
The company of prophets said to Elisha, “This place where we live here before you is too cramped for us.”
“Let us go to the Jordan and each cut a beam there, and let us make ourselves a place to live there.” He said, “Go.”
One of them spoke up and said, “If you are willing, go with your servants.” He said, “I will go.”
He went with them, and they came to the Jordan and cut down trees.
As one of them was felling a beam, his iron axe head fell into the water. He cried out and said, “Please, my master! Your servant borrowed it!”
The prophet of God said to him, “Where did it fall?” He showed him the place. He cut a piece of wood and threw it there, and the iron floated.
He said, “Pick up what is yours.” He reached out his hand and took it.
The king of Edom was at war with Israel. He consulted with his servants and said, “Set an ambush and hide in such-and-such a place.”
The prophet of God sent word to the king of Israel, saying, “Be careful not to pass through this place, because the Edomites are lying in ambush there.”
The king of Israel sent men to the place the prophet of God had told him about and warned him to beware of. This happened not just once or twice.
The king of Edom was deeply troubled by this matter. He called his servants and said to them, “Will you not tell me which of our people is on the side of the king of Israel?”
One of his servants answered, “None of our people is there, my lord the king. Rather, Elisha, the prophet of Israel, tells the king of Israel what you do in your bedroom.”
He said, “Go and see where he is, so that I can send men and capture him.” They reported to him, saying, “He is in Dothan.”
He sent horses, chariots, and a strong army there. They came by night and surrounded the town.
The servant of the prophet of God rose early to go out. He went out and saw an army surrounding the town, with horses and chariots. His young servant said to him, “Oh, my lord! How will we escape?”
He said to him, “Do not be afraid, because those who are with us are more numerous than those who are with them.”

Elisha prayed before the Lord and said, “Lord, open the young man’s eyes so that he may see.” The Lord opened the young man’s eyes, and he saw that the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
He went down to them, and Elisha prayed before the Lord and said, “Strike these people with blindness.” And he struck them with blindness, as Elisha had requested.
Elisha said to them, “This is not the road, and this is not the town. Follow me, and I will take you to the man you are looking for.” And he led them to Samaria.
When they entered Samaria, Elisha said, “Lord, open these people’s eyes so that they may see.” The Lord opened their eyes, and they saw that they were inside Samaria.
When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, “Shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down, my father?”
He said to him, “Do not kill them. Would you kill those you captured with your sword and bow? Set bread and water before them so that they may eat and drink and return to their master.”
He prepared a great feast for them, and they ate and drank and went back to their master. The raiding bands of Edom no longer came into the territory of Israel.
After this, Ben-hadad, king of Edom, gathered his whole army, marched up, camped against Samaria, and fought against it.
There was a severe famine in Samaria while they were besieging it, until a donkey’s head sold for eighty pieces of silver and a quarter of a kab of dove droppings for five pieces of silver.
The king of Israel was passing along the wall when a woman pleaded with him, saying, “Save me, my lord the king!”
He said to her, “May the Lord save you! Where could I find help for you—from the threshing floor or from the winepress?”
The king said to her, “What is the matter?” She said to him, “This woman said to me, ‘Give me your son so that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.’”
“So we cooked my son and ate him. The next day I said to her, ‘Give me your son so that we may eat him,’ but she hid her son.”
When the king heard the woman’s words as he was walking along the wall, he tore his clothes. The people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath, against his skin.
He said, “May God do this to me and more besides if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on him today!”

Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting before him. The king sent a man ahead of him. Before the messenger reached him, Elisha said to the elders, “Do you see that this murderer’s son has sent someone to take off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold it against him to keep him outside, for the sound of his master’s footsteps is behind him.”
While he was still speaking with them, the messenger came to him and said, “Look, this disaster is from the Lord! Why should I pray to the Lord any longer?”
Elisha said, “Hear the word of the Lord. This is what the Lord says: Tomorrow at this time, a seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria.”

The officer on whose hands the king leaned answered, “Even if the Lord made windows in heaven, could this happen?” He said to him, “You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it.”
Four men with leprosy were sitting outside the wall. They said to one another, “Why are we sitting here until we die?”

“If we decide to enter the town, the famine is severe inside the town, and we will die there. If we sit here, we will die. So come, let us go to the camp of Edom. If they spare us, we will live; if they kill us, we will die.”
They got up at dawn to go to the camp of Edom. They reached the edge of the camp, but no one was there.

The Lord had made the army of Edom hear the sound of horses, the sound of chariots, and the sound of a mighty army. They said to one another, “Look, the king of Israel has hired the king of the Egyptians and the king of the Hittites to come against us!”
They got up and fled at dawn, leaving their tents, their horses, their donkeys, and their camp just as it was, and fled for their lives.

Those men came to the edge of the camp and entered one tent. They ate and drank, took silver, gold, and clothes from there, and went away and hid them. Then they returned and entered another tent, took things from there, and went away and hid them.

They said to one another, “We are not doing what is right. Today is a day of good news. How long will we remain silent? If we wait until morning dawns, guilt will come upon us. Now come, let us go and report this to the royal household.”

They came and called to the city gatekeepers and told them, “We went to the camp of Edom, and there was no one there, nor any human voice—only horses tied up, donkeys tied up, and the tents just as they were.”
The gatekeepers called out and reported it inside the king’s palace.

The king got up during the night and said to his servants, “I will tell you what the Edomites have done to us. They know that we are starving, so they have left the camp to hide in the open country. They are saying, ‘When they come out of the city, we will capture them alive and enter the city.’”
One of his servants answered, “Let them take five of the remaining mounts. If they are captured, they will be counted like the whole army of Israel that has perished. Let us send them and see.”
They readied two teams of horses with chariots.

They followed them as far as the Jordan and saw that the whole road was full of clothing and equipment that the Edomites had abandoned in their haste. The messengers returned and reported to the king.
The people went out and plundered the camp of Edom. A seah of fine flour sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, just as the LORD had said.
The king put the officer on whose hands he leaned in charge of the gate. The people trampled him at the gate, and he died, just as the prophet of God had said when the messenger came down to him.
The prophet of God had told the king, “A seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, tomorrow at this time at the gates of Samaria.”
That officer had answered the prophet of God, “Even if the LORD made windows in heaven, could this happen?” He had told him, “You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it.”
And so it happened: the people trampled him at the gate, and he died.

Elisha said to the woman whose son he had restored to life, “Get up and go, you and your household, and settle wherever you can, because the LORD has called for a famine, and it will indeed come upon the land for seven years.”
The woman got up and did as the prophet of God had said. She and the members of her household went away, and she lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
After seven years she returned from the land of the Philistines and went to appeal to the king about her house and her field.
The king said to Gehazi, the servant of the prophet of God, “Tell me all the great things Elisha has done.”

While he was telling the king how he had restored a dead person to life, he saw the woman whose son he had restored to life appealing to the king about her house and her field. Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha restored to life.”

The king questioned the woman, and she told him. Then the king called an official and said to him, “Restore everything that belongs to her, including all the produce of her field from the day she left the land until now.”
Elisha came to Damascus while Ben-hadad king of Edom was ill. They informed him, saying, “The prophet of God has come here.”
The king said to Hazael, “Take a gift with you and go to meet the prophet of God. Ask him for the word of the LORD, and say to him, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”

Hazael went to meet him, taking with him a gift of all the good things of Damascus, a load for forty camels. He came and stood before him and said, “Your son Ben-hadad king of Edom has sent me to you, asking, ‘Will I survive this illness?’”
Elisha said to him, “Go and tell him, ‘You will certainly live.’ But the Lord has shown me that he will certainly die.”
And the prophet of God wept.

Hazael said, “Why is my lord weeping?” Elisha told him, “I know the harm you will do to the Israelites. You will burn their fortified towns with fire, kill their troops with the sword, dash their infants to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women.”
Hazael said, “What does your servant, a dog, amount to, that he should do such a great thing?” Elisha told him, “The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Edom.”
Hazael left Elisha and went to his master. His master asked him, “What did Elisha say to you?” He answered, “He told me that you will certainly live.”
The next day Hazael took a thick cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it over his face, and he died. Hazael became king in his place.
In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eight years.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, because Ahab’s sister was his wife. He did what was evil in the LORD’s sight.
But the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah because of his servant David, just as he had promised him that he would give a lamp to him and his descendants forever.
In his days Edom rebelled against Judah’s rule and appointed a king over themselves.

Joram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. He rose during the night to strike down the Edomites who were surrounding him and his commanders in their chariots, and the troops fled to their tents.
So Edom has remained in rebellion against Judah’s rule to this day. Libnah also rebelled at that time.
The rest of the acts of Joram, and everything he did, are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Joram rested with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Ahaziah became king after him.
In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Joram, king of Judah, began to reign.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for one year. His mother’s name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri king of Israel.
He followed the ways of the house of Ahab and did evil in the sight of the Lord, just as the house of Ahab had done, because he was related by marriage to the house of Ahab.
Joram son of Ahab went to war against Hazael king of Edom at Ramoth-gilead, and the Edomites wounded Joram.

Joram son of Ahab returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Edomites had inflicted on him at Ramoth while he was fighting Hazael king of Edom. Ahaziah king of Judah went down to see Joram son of Ahab, because he was ill in Jezreel.
The prophet Elisha called one of the members of the company of prophets and said to him, “Tuck your clothes into your belt, take this horn of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.
When you arrive there, look for Jehu son of Nimshi. Go in, have him get up from among his companions, and take him into an inner room.
Take the horn of oil, pour it on his head, and say to him, ‘This is what the Lord says: I have anointed you to be king over my people Israel.’ Then open the door and flee. Do not delay.”
So the young prophet went to Ramoth-gilead.
He went in and saw the army commanders sitting together. He said, “I have a message to tell you, commander.” Jehu asked, “For which of us?” He answered, “For you, commander.”
Jehu got up and went into the room. The man poured oil on his head and said to him, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: I have anointed you to reign over the Lord’s people, over Israel.
You shall strike down the house of Ahab your master, and I will take vengeance on Jezebel for the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the Lord’s servants.”
I will destroy the whole house of Ahab. I will destroy every male of Ahab’s house who urinates against a wall, both bound and free in Israel.
I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
Dogs will eat Jezebel on the estate at Jezreel, and no one will bury her.” Then he opened the door and fled.
Jehu went out to his master’s servants, and they asked him, “Is everything all right? Why did this madman come to you?” He said to them, “You know the man and his madness.”
They said to him, “You are lying! Tell us.” He said to them, “This is what he told me: ‘This is what the Lord says: I have anointed you to reign over Israel.’”
They hurried, each taking his cloak and spreading it beneath him on the landing of the steps. They blew the trumpet and said, “Jehu is king!”
Jehu son of Nimshi rebelled against Joram. Joram and all Israel with him had been defending Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Edom.

King Joram had returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Edomites had inflicted on him while he was fighting Hazael king of Edom. Jehu said, “If this is what you want, let no one escape from the city to go and report it in Jezreel.”
Jehu mounted his chariot and went there, because Joram was lying there ill. Ahaziah king of Judah had gone down to see Joram son of Ahab, because he was ill in Jezreel.

The watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel and saw Jehu’s company approaching. The watchman said, “I see riders.” Joram said, “Take a chariot and send it to meet them, and have its driver ask, ‘Is there peace?’”

A horseman went to meet him and said to him, “This is what the king asks: ‘Is there peace?’” Jehu said, “What have you to do with peace? Turn around and follow me.” The watchman reported, “The messenger has reached them, but he has not returned.”
He sent another horseman to them, who said, “This is what the king asks: ‘Is there peace?’” Jehu said, “What have you to do with peace? Turn around and follow me.”
The watchman reported, “The messenger has reached them, but he has not returned. The driving is like that of Jehu son of Nimshi, because he drives furiously.”

Joram said, “Harness the chariots!” They harnessed the chariots, and Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his own chariot. They went out to meet Jehu and encountered him on the property of Naboth the Jezreelite.
When Joram saw Jehu, he asked him, “Is there peace, Jehu?” Jehu answered him, “What peace can there be with the prostitution of your mother Jezebel or her many acts of sorcery?”
Joram turned around and fled, saying to Ahaziah, “Treachery, Ahaziah!”
Jehu drew his bow with all his strength and struck Joram between the shoulders. The arrow went through his heart, and he slumped down in his chariot.

Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, “Pick him up and throw him onto the property of Naboth the Jezreelite. For I remember when you and I were riding together behind his father Ahab, and the Lord pronounced this word against him.”

“Surely I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons last evening,” says the Lord, “and I will repay you on this plot of land,” says the Lord. “Now take him and throw him onto this plot of land, according to the Lord’s word.” So they threw him onto the plot belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite.

When Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled along the road to Beth-haggan. Jehu pursued him and said, “Kill him too!” They struck him down in his chariot at the ascent of Gud, beside Ibleam. He fled to Megiddo and died there.
His servants picked him up, brought him to Jerusalem, and buried him in a tomb with his ancestors in the City of David.
In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah became king over Judah.
Jehu came to Jezreel. When Jezebel heard, she painted her eyes with eye makeup, arranged her hair, and looked out of the window.
As Jehu entered the gate, she said, “Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of your master?”
He looked up toward the window and said, “Who is with me?” Two or three eunuchs appeared at the window before him.
He said, “Throw her down!” They threw her down, and some of her blood splashed onto the wall. The horses came over her and trampled her.
He went inside to eat and drink, and said, “Attend to that cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king’s daughter.”
They went to bury her, but found nothing of her except her head, her feet, and the palms of her hands.
They returned and told him, and he said, “This is the Lord’s word, which he spoke through his servant Elijah from Tishbe: ‘On the plot of land at Jezreel, dogs will eat Jezebel’s flesh.
Jezebel’s corpse will be like dung on the surface of the ground on the plot of land at Jezreel, with no one to bury her, so that no one will say, “This is Jezebel.”’”

Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria, and the city’s leading men were raising them. Jehu wrote a letter and sent it to Samaria, to the leading men, the elders, and the guardians of Ahab’s children, saying:
“As soon as this letter reaches you, since your masters’ sons are with you, and you have chariots, horses, fortified towns, and weapons,
choose whichever of your masters’ sons you consider good and suitable, put him on his father’s throne, and fight for your masters’ household.”
When the men heard this, they were very afraid and said, “Look, two kings could not stand against him. How can we stand?”

The palace administrator, the governor of the city, the elders, and the guardians sent word to Jehu: “We are your servants, and we will do everything you tell us. We will not make anyone king over us. Do whatever seems good to you.”

He wrote them a second letter, saying, “If you are on my side and obey me, take the heads of your masters’ sons and bring them to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow.” Now the king’s sons numbered seventy men, and the city’s leading men were raising them.
When the letter arrived, they took the king’s sons and slaughtered them, seventy men. They put their heads in baskets and sent them to him at Jezreel.
A messenger came and told him, “They have brought the heads of the king’s sons.” He said, “Pile them in two heaps at the entrance to the gate until morning.”
In the morning he went out and said to all the people, “You are innocent. If I rebelled against my master and killed him, who killed all these?
Know, then, that none of the Lord’s word will fall to the ground unfulfilled—nothing of all that the Lord said against Ahab’s household. The Lord has done what he spoke through his servant Elijah.”
Jehu destroyed everyone belonging to Ahab’s household who was found in Jezreel, along with all his leading men, his relatives, and his priests. He left him no survivor.
He set out and went into Samaria, and he was removing the burnt offerings along the road.
Jehu met the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah and asked them, “Who are you?” They told him, “We are Ahaziah’s brothers, and we have come down to greet the king’s sons and the queen’s sons.”
He said, “Capture them alive!” They captured them, slaughtered them, and threw them into the pit, forty-two men. He did not leave a single one of them alive.

He went on from there and met Jehonadab son of Rechab, who was coming to meet him. He greeted him and said, “Is your heart as sincere toward mine as mine is toward yours?” Jehonadab said, “Yes, indeed.” He said to him, “Give me your hand.” He gave him his hand, and he helped him up beside him into the chariot.
He said to him, “Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD.” He seated him beside him in the chariot.
He entered Samaria and struck down everyone belonging to Ahab’s household who was found in Samaria, until he had destroyed them, according to the Lord’s word spoken by Elijah.
Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, “Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him a great deal.”

“Now summon to me all Baal’s prophets, all his priests, and all his worshipers. Let no one fail to come, because I am offering a great sacrifice to Baal. Anyone who fails to come will not live.” Jehu did this deceitfully, intending to destroy Baal’s worshipers.
Jehu said, “Summon the whole assembly for Baal.” And they summoned it.
Jehu sent word throughout Israel, and all Baal’s worshipers came. Not a single person stayed away. They entered Baal’s temple, and Baal’s temple was filled from end to end.
He said to the treasurer, “Bring out garments for all of them.”
Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab entered Baal’s temple. Jehu said to Baal’s worshipers, “Search and make sure that none of the Lord’s servants are here among you, but only Baal’s worshipers.”

They went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Jehu stationed three hundred and eighty men outside at the gate and said, “If any of the men I am handing over to you escapes, the life of the man who lets him escape will be taken in place of his life.”

When they had finished offering the sacrifices and burnt offerings, Jehu said to the guards and warriors, “Go in and kill them. Do not let any of them escape.” They killed them with the sword, and the guards and warriors threw them down and went as far as the town of the temple of Baal.
They brought out the sacred pillar of the temple of Baal and burned it in the fire.
He tore down Baal’s sacred pillar, and they demolished the temple of Baal and made it a latrine, as it remains to this day.
Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.
Nevertheless, Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin: the golden calves at Bethel and Dan.

The LORD said to Jehu, “Because you have done what is right in my sight and have done to the house of Ahab everything that was in my heart, your descendants will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.”
But Jehu did not take care to follow the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
In those days the LORD began to afflict Israel, and Hazael attacked them throughout the territory of Israel.
From the Jordan eastward, this included all the land of Gilead, Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh, from Aroer on the bank of the Arnon Valley, including Gilead and Bashan.
The rest of Jehu’s deeds, everything he did, and all his mighty acts are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jehu died and joined his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz became king in his place.
Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty-eight years.
When Athaliah, Ahaziah’s mother, saw that her son was dead, she set out to destroy the entire royal family.

Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king’s sons who were being killed. She hid him and his nurse in his bedroom. She hid him from Athaliah, and he did not die.
He remained hidden with her in the house of the LORD for six years, while Athaliah ruled over the land.

In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest sent for the commanders of hundreds, the guards, and the bodyguards, and brought them to him in the house of the LORD. He stationed them in the house of the LORD, made a covenant with them, exchanged oaths with them, and showed them the king’s son.
He commanded them, saying, “This is what you must do: a third of you who come on duty on the Sabbath must keep watch over the king’s palace.
a third at the gate of [?], and a third at the gate of the guards’ quarters. Guard the palace against any intrusion.
The two divisions of you who go off duty on the Sabbath must guard the house of the LORD along with those of the king’s palace.
Surround the king, each man with his weapon in his hand. Anyone who enters the ranks must die. Stay with the king when he goes out and when he comes in.”

The commanders of hundreds did as Jehoiada the priest commanded them. Each took his men, those coming on duty on the Sabbath together with those going off duty on the Sabbath, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and shields of King David that were in the house of the LORD.
The guards stood, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the temple to the left side of the temple, and surrounded the altar and the king’s palace.
They brought out the king’s son and put a crown on his head, [?] the testimony. They anointed him and made him king, clapped their hands, and said, “Long live the king!”
Athaliah heard the noise of the crowd and the people rejoicing, and she came to the people at the house of the LORD.

She saw the king standing by the pillar, as was the custom for kings, with the officials and horn blowers standing before the king. All the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing horns. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, “Treason! Treason!”

Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds who were in charge of the army, saying, “Take her outside the ranks, and anyone who follows her must be killed with the sword.” For the priest had said, “She must not be killed in the house of the LORD.”
Room was made for her, and she went along the road to the entrance used by the king’s horses. There she died.
Jehoiada the priest established a covenant between the LORD and the people, that they should be the LORD’s people, and [?] between the king and the people.

All the people of the land entered the temple of Baal, tore down his altars, and smashed his images. They killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, in front of the altar. The priest appointed overseers over the house of the LORD.

He took the commanders of hundreds, the guards, the bodyguards, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD. He entered the king’s palace by way of the Gate of the Guards and sat on the royal throne.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. They had killed Athaliah with the sword.
Joash was seven years old when he became king.
Joash became king in the seventh year of Jehu, and he reigned in Jerusalem for forty years. His mother’s name was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
Joash did what was right before the LORD throughout the time that Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
However, he did not remove the high places. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places.

Joash said to the priests, “All the consecrated money brought into the house of the LORD—the money a person gives to ransom his life, and all the money anyone decides in his heart to bring into the house of the LORD—
the priests are to receive, each from whoever is willing to give. They are to spend it on repairing the temple wherever damage is found.”
But by the twenty-third year of King Joash, the priests had not repaired the damage to the house.

King Joash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, “Why are you not repairing the damage to the temple? Now stop taking money from those who give it to you; hand it over for the repair of the temple.”
The priests agreed not to take money from the people and not to repair the damage to the temple.

Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and placed it beside the altar, on the right as a person enters the house of the LORD. The priests who guarded the entrances put into it all the money brought into the house of the LORD.

When they saw that there was a large amount of money in the chest, the king’s secretary went up with the high priest. They went up, counted, and tied up in bags the money found in the house of the LORD.
They gave the money, tied up in bags, to those supervising the work in the house of the LORD, and they gave it to the carpenters and builders working in the house of the LORD.
And to the builders and stonecutters, to buy timber and dressed stones to repair the damage to the house of the Lord, and for every expense incurred in strengthening the building.
But no silver basins, snuffers, bowls, trumpets, or any gold or silver utensils were made for the house of the Lord from the money brought into the house of the Lord.
Instead, they gave it to the workers, who used it to repair the LORD’s temple.
They did not require an accounting from the men who were given the money to pay the workers, because they faithfully paid out the money for the repairs.
The offering money and the money for sin offerings were not brought into the LORD’s temple; they belonged to the priests.
Then Hazael king of Edom went up, fought against Gath, and captured it. Hazael then set his sights on marching against Jerusalem.

Joash king of Judah took the sacred gifts dedicated by his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, kings of Judah, together with his own sacred gifts and all the gold found in the treasury of the house of the Lord and in the royal palace. He sent them to Hazael king of Edom, who withdrew from Jerusalem.
The rest of the acts of Joash and everything he did are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Joash’s servants rose up in rebellion and killed Joash at Beth Millo as he was going down to Sela.
His servants Jozacar son of Shimeath and Jozabar son of Shamir struck him down, and he died. He was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, and his son Amaziah became king after him.
In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria. He reigned for seventeen years.
He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord and followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin. He did not turn away from them.
The Lord's anger burned against Israel, and he handed them over to Hazael king of Edom and to Ben-hadad son of Hazael throughout that time.
Jehoahaz prayed before the Lord, and the Lord heard him, because he saw the oppression of Israel, how the king of Edom oppressed them.
The Lord gave Israel a deliverer, and they escaped from the power of Edom. The Israelites lived peacefully in their tents as they had before.
Nevertheless, they did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, but continued to follow them. The idol also remained standing in Samaria.
Jehoahaz was left with no troops except fifty horsemen, twenty chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, because the king of Edom had destroyed them and made them like dust to be trampled.
The rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, everything he did, and his mighty deeds are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jehoahaz died and joined his ancestors. He was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoash succeeded him as king.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, became king over Israel in Samaria. He reigned for thirteen years.
He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, but continued to follow them.
The rest of the acts of Jehoash, everything he did, his mighty deeds, and how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jehoash died and rested with his ancestors, and his son Jeroboam sat on his throne. Jehoash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
Elisha became sick with the illness from which he died. Jehoash king of Israel went down to him, wept over him, and said, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!"
Elisha said to him, “Take a bow and arrows.” So he took a bow and arrows.
He said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand on the bow." He put his hand on it, and Elisha placed his hands over the king's hands.

He said, "Open the window toward the east," and he opened it. Elisha said to him, "Shoot!" He shot an arrow, and Elisha said, "The Lord's arrow of deliverance, an arrow of deliverance against Edom! You will strike down the Edomites at Aphek until you destroy them completely."
He said to him, “Take an arrow,” and he took one. He said, “Strike the ground.” He struck three times and stopped.

The prophet of God became angry with him and said, "You should have struck five or six times! Then you would have struck down the Edomites until you destroyed them completely. But now you will strike Edom only three times."
Elisha died, and they buried him. Moabite raiding bands came into the land that same year.
While they were burying a man, they saw a raiding band and threw the man into Elisha's tomb. The man came into contact with Elisha's bones, came to life, and stood on his feet.
Hazael king of Edom oppressed Israel throughout the days of Jehoahaz.

But the Lord was gracious to them, had compassion on them, and turned toward them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The Lord was unwilling to destroy them, and up to that time he had not cast them out of his presence.
Hazael king of Edom died, and his son Ben-hadad became king after him.
Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the towns that he had taken from his father Jehoahaz in battle. Jehoash defeated him for three years and restored those towns to Israel.
In the second year of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother's name was Jehoaddin, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right before the Lord, though not like his ancestor David. He did as his father Joash had done.
However, he did not remove the high places, and the people were still sacrificing and burning incense at the high places.
When the kingdom was firmly under his control, he killed the servants who had killed his father, King Joash.

But he did not kill the murderers' children, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses, where the Lord commanded, saying, "Fathers must not die because of their children, and children must not die because of their fathers. Rather, each person must die for his own sins."
He struck down twenty thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. He also defeated Sela in battle and named it Nakthael, its name to this day.
Then Amaziah king of Judah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us face one another in battle."

Jehoash king of Israel sent word to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, "The thornbush in Lebanon sent word to the cedar in Lebanon: 'Give your daughter to my son as his wife.' But a wild animal in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thornbush.
You have indeed defeated Edom, and your heart has made you proud. Enjoy your honor and stay at home. Do not provoke disaster and fall, taking Judah down with you."
But Amaziah would not listen to him. Jehoash king of Israel and Amaziah king of Judah went up and faced one another at Beth-shemesh in Judah—he and Amaziah king of Judah.
Judah was defeated before Israel, and each man fled to his tent.
Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah at Beth-shemesh. He entered Jerusalem and broke down four hundred cubits of Jerusalem's wall, from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.
He took all the gold and silver and all the utensils found in the house of the Lord and in the king's treasury, as well as hostages, and returned to Samaria.
The rest of the deeds of Jehoash, everything he did, his mighty deeds, and how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jehoash rested with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. His son Jeroboam succeeded him as king.
Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Amaziah are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
They rebelled against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. They sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.
They carried him back on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the City of David.
All the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah after the king rested with his ancestors.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Jehoash, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, began to reign in Samaria. He reigned for forty-one years.
He did what was evil in the Lord's sight. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, but continued in them.

He restored Israel's territory from the entrance to Hamath as far as the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the Lord, the God of Israel, which he spoke through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.
For the Lord saw that Israel's oppression was very bitter, and there was no one to bind or release, nor anyone to help Israel.
The Lord had not said that he would wipe out Israel's name from under heaven, so he saved them through Jeroboam son of Jehoash, son of Jehoahaz.
The rest of the deeds of Jeroboam, everything he did, his mighty deeds, and how he fought and restored Damascus and Hamath to Israel are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Jeroboam rested with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors, with the kings of Israel. His son Zechariah succeeded him as king.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Uzziah son of Amaziah, king of Judah, began to reign.
He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned in Jerusalem for fifty-two years. His mother's name was Jeconiah, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the sight of the Lord, as his father Amaziah had done.
However, he did not remove the high places. The people were still offering sacrifices and burning incense at the high places.
The Lord struck the king, and he had leprosy until the day he died. He lived in a house in seclusion, while Jotham, the king's son, was in charge of the palace and governed the people of the land.
The rest of Uzziah’s acts and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Uzziah died and rested with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Jotham became king in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Uzziah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for six months.
He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his father had done. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
Shallum son of Jabesh rebelled against him, struck him down in front of the people, killed him, and became king in his place.
The rest of Zechariah’s deeds are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
The word of the Lord that he had spoken to Jehu was fulfilled: “Your descendants down to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel.” And so it happened.
Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned in Samaria for one month.
Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and entered Samaria. He struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria, killed him, and became king in his place.
The rest of Shallum’s acts and the rebellion he carried out are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Then Menahem attacked Tiphsah, everyone in it, and its territory, starting from Tirzah, because they had not opened the gate to him. He destroyed it and ripped open all its pregnant women.
In the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for ten years.
He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord. Throughout his life he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.
Pul king of Assyria came against the land. Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver so that he would support him and secure the kingdom in his hands.

Menahem levied the silver on Israel, on all the wealthy men of the land, to give to the king of Assyria: fifty shekels of silver from each man. Then the king of Assyria withdrew and did not remain there in the land.
The rest of Menahem’s acts and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
Menahem rested with his ancestors, and his son Pekahiah became king in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Uzziah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for two years.
He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord and did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

Pekah son of Remaliah, his warrior, rebelled against him and killed him in Samaria, in the enclosure of the royal palace. He took Argob and Ani, and fifty men from Gilead were with him. He killed him and became king in his place.
The rest of Pekahiah’s acts and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Uzziah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for twenty years.
He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord and did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and captured Ijon, Abel-meholah, all Beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee, and the whole land of Naphtali. He deported their people to Assyria.
Hoshea son of Elah rebelled against Pekah son of Remaliah, struck him down, killed him, and became king in his place in the second year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
The rest of Pekah’s acts and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah became king of Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for sixteen years. His mother’s name was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right before the Lord, just as his father Uzziah had done.
However, he did not remove the high places. The people still offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places. He built the Upper Gate of the house of the Lord.
The rest of Jotham’s acts and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
In those days the LORD began to stir up Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, against Judah.
Jotham rested with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Ahaz became king in his place.
In the eighteenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, Ahaz son of Jotham, king of Judah, began to reign.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for sixteen years. He did not do what was right before the LORD his God, as his ancestor David had done.
He followed the ways of the kings of Israel. He even made his son pass through fire, according to the custom of the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before the Israelites.
He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills, and under every leafy tree.
Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to fight against him, but they could not fight against him.
At that time Rezin king of Aram restored Elath to Aram and drove Judah out of Elath. The Arameans came to Elath and settled there, where they remain to this day.
Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, “I am your servant and your son. Come up and rescue me from the king of Aram and the king of Israel, who are rising against me.”
Ahaz took the silver and gold found in the LORD’s house and in the king’s treasury and sent them as a gift to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria listened to him. The king of Assyria marched against Damascus, captured it, deported its people to Kir, and killed Rezin.

King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria. He saw the altar in Damascus, and King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest a likeness of the altar, its design, and all the details of its workmanship.
Uriah the priest made an altar according to what King Ahaz had sent from Damascus. Uriah the priest made it this way before King Ahaz returned from Damascus.
The king returned from Damascus, and King Ahaz saw the altar. The king approached the altar and went up onto it.
He offered burnt offerings and offerings on it, poured out drink offerings, and splashed the blood of his fellowship offerings on the altar.
He moved the bronze altar that stood before the LORD away from the front of the house, from between the altar and the LORD’s house, and placed it on the north side of the altar.

King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, saying to him, “On the large altar offer the morning burnt offering, the evening offering, the king’s burnt offering and his offering, and the burnt offering of all the people of the land, together with their offerings and drink offerings. Sprinkle on it all the blood of the burnt offerings and all the blood of the sacrifices. The bronze altar will be for me to inquire by.”
Uriah the priest did as King Ahaz commanded him.
King Ahaz cut off the side panels of the stands and removed the basins from them. He lowered the Sea from the bronze oxen and placed it on a stone pavement.
He altered the Sabbath shelter that he had built in the LORD’s house and the entrance of the outer gate at the LORD’s house because of the king of Assyria.
The rest of the acts of Ahaz and everything he did are recorded in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
Ahaz rested with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Hezekiah became king in his place.
In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king over Israel in Samaria and reigned for nine years.
He did what was evil in the Lord’s sight, but not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him, and Hoshea became his servant and brought him tribute.

The king of Assyria discovered rebellion in Hoshea: Hoshea had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and had not brought tribute to the king of Assyria as he had done every year. So the king of Assyria detained him and confined him in prison.
The king of Assyria invaded the whole land, came up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and deported the Israelites to Assyria. He settled them in Halah, on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of Media.
This happened when the Israelites sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt from under the power of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and worshiped other gods.
They followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had destroyed before the Israelites.
The Israelites and their kings spoke things that were not right against the LORD their God. They built high places for themselves in all their towns, from watchtowers to fortified cities.
They set up sacred pillars and idols for themselves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
They burned incense there on the high places, like the nations whom the LORD had destroyed before them. They did evil things, provoking the LORD to anger.
They served idols, concerning which the Lord had told them, “You must not do this.”

The LORD warned Israel and Judah through all his servants the prophets and through all the seers, saying, “Turn back from your evil ways and keep my commandments and my statutes, according to the laws I commanded your ancestors and according to what I sent to them through my servants the prophets.”
But they did not listen. They were more stubborn than their ancestors and did not trust in the Lord their God.

They rejected my covenants and my commandments that I commanded their ancestors, and the warnings I gave them. They followed worthless things and gained nothing. Instead, they followed the nations concerning whom the LORD had commanded them, “Do not do as they do.”
They abandoned all the commandments of the LORD their God and made themselves cast images, two calves. They offered sacrifices to idols, bowed down to all the host of heaven, and served Baal.
They made their sons and daughters pass through fire, practiced divination, interpreted omens, and planned to do everything evil in the LORD’s sight, provoking him to anger.
The LORD became very angry with Israel and removed them from his presence. Only the tribe of Judah remained.
The people of Judah also failed to keep the commandments of the LORD their God. They followed Israel’s practices, doing evil in the LORD’s sight and provoking him to anger continually.
The LORD rejected all the descendants of Israel, humbled them, and handed them over to plunderers until he cast them out of his presence.
For the house of Israel broke away from following David and made Jeroboam son of Nebat king over themselves. Jeroboam led Israel away from following the LORD and caused them to commit great sins.
The Israelites followed all the sins that Jeroboam had committed and did not turn away from them,
Eventually the LORD removed Israel from his presence, just as the LORD had declared through all the prophets. He exiled the people of Israel from their land to Assyria, where they remain to this day.

The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim and settled them in the towns of Samaria in place of the Israelites. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its towns.
When they first settled there, they did not fear the LORD. So the LORD sent lions among them, which began killing them.

They reported to the king of Assyria, saying, “The nations you exiled and settled in the towns of Samaria do not know the requirements of the god of the land. He has sent lions among them, and now they are killing them because they do not know the requirements of the god of the land.”
The king of Assyria commanded, “Take back there one of the priests you exiled from there. Let him go and live there and teach them the requirements of the god of the land.”
One of the priests who had been exiled from Samaria came and settled in Bethel. He taught them how to fear the LORD.
Each nation served its own god, and they left the shrines of the high places that they had made in Samaria, each nation in its own towns where its people lived.
The people of Babylon served Succoth-benoth, the people of Cuthah served Nergal, and the people of Hamath served Ashima.
The Avvites served Ibzah and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burned their sons in fire to Adrammelech and Amalek, the gods of Sepharvaim.
They feared the LORD, and they appointed from among themselves priests of the high places, who ministered for them in the shrine of the high places.
They feared the LORD, but they also served their own gods according to the practices of the nations. And they exiled the Israelites from their land.

To this day, because they have abandoned the LORD, they follow the practices of the nations. They do not fear the LORD or act according to the covenant, the judgments, the law, or the commandment that the LORD commanded the descendants of Jacob, whom he named Israel.
The LORD made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, “Do not fear other gods, bow down to them, serve them, or offer sacrifices to them.
Instead, serve the LORD, who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great power and an uplifted arm. Serve him, bow down to him, and offer sacrifices to him.
Keep and carry out the covenants, judgments, laws, and commandments that he wrote for you, every day. Do not fear other gods.”
Do not forget the covenants that I made with you, and do not fear the gods of the nations.
Instead, fear the Lord your God, and he will rescue you from the power of all your enemies.”
But they did not listen; instead, they continued to follow their former customs.

These nations that settled in Samaria also feared the LORD, but they continued serving their carved images. Their children and their grandchildren did the same: just as their ancestors had done, so they too have continued doing to this day.
In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-nine years. His mother’s name was Aki, daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right before the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.

He removed the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, cut down the idols, and cut up the bronze serpent that Moses had made. For the Israelites had gone astray by following it and had been offering incense to it until those days. They called it Nehushtan.
He trusted in the Lord, the God of Israel. Among all the kings of Judah, there was no one like him after him, nor among those who came before him.
He held fast to the Lord and did not turn away from following him. He kept his commandments, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord was with him, and wherever he went he was victorious. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and would not serve him.
He defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its surrounding territory, from the watchtower to the fortified city.
In the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah, king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria marched against Samaria and besieged it.
He captured it after three years. In the sixth year of Hezekiah king of Judah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was captured.
The king of Assyria deported Israel to Assyria and settled them in Halah, on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of Media.
This happened because they had not obeyed the Lord their God but had broken his covenant. They neither listened to nor carried out everything that Moses, the servant of the Lord, had commanded them.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria marched against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

Hezekiah king of Judah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, “I have done wrong. Withdraw from me, and I will bear whatever you impose on me.” The king of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
Hezekiah gave all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasury of the royal palace.
At that time Hezekiah stripped the doors of the house of the Lord and the thresholds that Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gave them to the king of Assyria.

The king of Assyria again sent the commander-in-chief, the chief cupbearer, and the chief eunuch from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem with a powerful army. They marched against Jerusalem and stood at the conduit of the upper pool, on the road to the fuller's field.
They called for the king, and Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary, and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came out to them.
The chief cupbearer said to them, “Tell Hezekiah: This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this confidence on which you rely?
You have said that you have words on your lips, and strategy and strength for war. Now, on whom have you relied, that you have rebelled against me?

Look, you have relied on Egypt, that splintered reed of a staff. When a man leans on it, it goes into his hand and pierces it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is like to everyone who relies on him.
If you tell me, ‘We rely on the Lord our God,’ is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, telling Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship before one altar in Jerusalem’?
